answer: A harbor master does not trust every ship that claims a berth. Each agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers prove it forged an identity. A newcomer arrives like a comet, bright, fast and unproven, and earns trust only by completing small verified jobs over time, while a sparrow-sized stake lets honest small agents join without locking out the poor. Copying an identity costs a fresh stake each time, so flooding the market with fakes burns money faster than it earns, and the harbor's shared ledger makes every burnt stake visible to all.
